meta.name: PhysAlts Timeline of Physics
meta.description: Fact-checked chronological atlas of physics milestones from Old Babylonian mathematical astronomy (c. 1800 BCE) through upcoming 2045+ mega-experiments.

eras.label: Pre-Classical & Ancient Foundations
eras.summary: Quantitative astronomy, metrology, optics, statics, hydrostatics, and naturalistic cosmology across Mesopotamia, Egypt, India, China, and the Mediterranean.

eras.label: Golden Ages & Medieval Optics
eras.summary: Experimental optics, magnetism, algebra of motion, and precision observatories across the Islamic Golden Age, Song China, India, and medieval Europe.

eras.label: Scientific Revolution
eras.summary: Heliocentrism, telescopic astronomy, laws of planetary motion, universal gravitation, calculus, and analytical mechanics.

eras.label: Electromagnetism & Thermodynamics
eras.summary: Unification of electricity, magnetism, and light; statistical entropy; X-rays; and the discovery of radioactivity.

eras.label: Relativity & Quantum Century
eras.summary: Spacetime curvature, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, QED, semiconductor electronics, cosmic microwave background, and the Standard Model.

eras.label: Precision & Mega-Experiments
eras.summary: High-Tc superconductors, Bose-Einstein condensates, neutrino mass, dark energy, graphene, Higgs boson, gravitational waves, black hole imaging, and fusion ignition.

eras.label: Upcoming Frontier (2027–2045+)
eras.summary: Next-generation compact and burning-plasma fusion, 39 m optical telescopes, gigaton neutrino observatories, space interferometers, and post-LHC colliders.

events.title: Old Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy, Venus Tablet & Plimpton 322
events.summary: Compiled systematic 21-year synodic observations of Venus (Tablet of Ammisaduqa) alongside base-60 exact Pythagorean-triple tables (Plimpton 322), establishing predictive mathematical astronomy and sexagesimal angular measurement.
events.impact: Created the 360-degree circle, 60-minute hour, and quantitative planetary period tracking inherited by Greek and later astronomy.

events.title: Rhind Mathematical Papyrus: Egyptian Metrology, Slope & Mechanics
events.summary: Recorded 84 worked problems in arithmetic, geometric area/volume estimation, and the seked (incline ratio) used in precision surveying, solar alignment, and monumental engineering.
events.impact: Demonstrated systematic quantitative problem-solving and standardized physical measurement over a millennium before classical Greece.

events.title: Vedanga Jyotisha & Sulba Sutras: Calendar Astronomy & Geometry
events.summary: Formulated quantitative luni-solar timekeeping rules tracking solstices and lunar mansions (Vedanga Jyotisha) alongside explicit geometric statements of the Pythagorean relation and √2 approximations (Sulba Sutras).
events.impact: Established South Asia's continuous mathematical astronomy and computational geometry tradition.

events.title: Anaximander's Free-Floating Earth & Naturalistic Cosmology
events.summary: Anaximander proposed that Earth hangs unsupported in space by symmetry rather than resting on pillars or water, explaining rain, wind, and celestial motion through natural law.
events.impact: Pioneered naturalistic cosmology in the Mediterranean world, explaining cosmic equilibrium through symmetry rather than myth.

events.title: Mozi & the Mohist Canon: Camera Obscura, Optics & Inertia
events.summary: In the Mo Jing (Mohist Canon), described rectilinear propagation of light, inverted pinhole images (camera obscura), focal properties of concave and convex mirrors, and the persistence of motion absent opposing forces.
events.impact: Recorded the earliest known systematic treatise on geometrical optics and pinhole image formation.

events.title: Aristarchus of Samos: Heliocentric Model & Cosmic Distances
events.summary: Proposed a heliocentric model placing the Sun at the center with Earth rotating daily and orbiting annually, and used lunar-phase geometry to estimate relative Sun-Moon sizes and distances.
events.impact: Demonstrated trigonometric cosmic distance measurement and anticipated Copernican heliocentrism by 1,800 years.

events.title: Archimedes' Principle, Statics & Law of the Lever
events.summary: Formulated exact mathematical laws of buoyancy (On Floating Bodies), centers of gravity, levers, and early exhaustion methods anticipating integral calculus.
events.impact: Established mathematical physics as a rigorous deductive discipline bridging geometry and mechanics.

events.title: Eratosthenes Measures Earth's Circumference
events.summary: Compared the summer solstice noon zenith Sun in Syene (Aswan) with a 7.2° shadow angle in Alexandria to calculate Earth's circumference to within a few percent of the true 40,075 km value.
events.impact: Founded mathematical geodesy and proved that planetary scales can be measured via simple geometric experiments.

events.title: Aryabhatiya: Earth's Rotation & Eclipse Mechanics
events.summary: In the Aryabhatiya, Aryabhata explained the apparent westward motion of the stars via Earth's axial rotation and gave a quantitative shadow-based model of solar and lunar eclipses.
events.impact: Laid mathematical and astronomical foundations for Indian and Islamic planetary science.

events.title: Brahmasphutasiddhanta: Arithmetic of Zero & Gravitational Attraction
events.summary: Formalized rules for zero and negative numbers while describing Earth's innate property of attracting all bodies toward itself (gurutvakarshan).
events.impact: Provided essential mathematical notation and planetary computation methods transmitted to Baghdad and Europe.

events.title: Kitab al-Manazir (Book of Optics) & Experimental Method
events.summary: Proved via controlled camera obscura and pinhole experiments that vision occurs when light rays enter the eye from illuminated objects, analyzing reflection and refraction quantitatively.
events.impact: Pioneered systematic experimental verification and shaped European optics for six centuries.

events.title: Dream Pool Essays: Magnetic Declination & Focal Optics
events.summary: Described the magnetic needle compass, discovered true magnetic declination relative to geographic north, and analyzed focal points of concave mirrors and pinhole image inversion.
events.impact: Recorded the earliest known quantitative observations of geomagnetism and practical compass navigation.

events.title: Siddhanta Shiromani: Instantaneous Motion & Planetary Speeds
events.summary: Introduced tatkalika gati (instantaneous velocity) to compute planetary positions and stated that a vanishing derivative occurs at extrema, anticipating differential calculus.
events.impact: Advanced mathematical kinematics and spherical astronomy centuries before European calculus.

events.title: Robert Grosseteste's De Luce & Mathematical Optics
events.summary: Argued that physical nature must be understood through geometry and light (De Luce) and formulated a method of resolution and composition using controlled observation.
events.impact: Inspired the Oxford scientific tradition connecting mathematical physics with empirical testing.

events.title: Maragheh Observatory & the Tusi Couple
events.summary: Founded a state-funded international research observatory equipped with giant mural quadrants and developed the Tusi couple, generating linear motion from two uniform circular motions.
events.impact: Produced the Ilkhanic Tables and planetary geometric mechanisms later echoed in Copernican astronomy.

events.title: Opus Majus: Scientia Experimentalis & Lenses
events.summary: Synthesized Ibn al-Haytham's optics with European scholarship in Opus Majus, advocating experimental science, quantitative measurement of the rainbow angle (42°), and magnifying lenses.
events.impact: Championed empirical verification as the foundation of natural philosophy in Western Europe.

events.title: Rainbow Refraction Explained with Water-Filled Glass Spheres
events.summary: Used water-filled spherical flasks as single raindrops to demonstrate experimentally that primary rainbows arise from two refractions and one internal reflection, and secondary rainbows from two internal reflections.
events.impact: Solved the geometric optics of the rainbow in parallel with Kamal al-Din al-Farisi, centuries before Descartes.

events.title: Ulugh Beg Observatory & Zij-i-Sultani Star Catalogue
events.summary: Constructed a monumental 40-meter subterranean marble Fakhri sextant measuring Earth's axial tilt (23°30'17") and the sidereal year to within one minute of modern values.
events.impact: Compiled the most accurate naked-eye star catalogue of the pre-telescopic era (992 stars).

events.title: De Revolutionibus: Heliocentric Solar System
events.summary: Published a comprehensive mathematical model placing the Sun rather than Earth at the center of the planetary system, explaining retrograde planetary loops naturally.
events.impact: Triggered the Copernican Revolution that transformed astronomy and human cosmology.

events.title: Telescopic Observations & Foundations of Kinematics
events.summary: Turned an improved refracting telescope skyward, discovering Jupiter's four largest moons, lunar craters, sunspots, and Venusian phases alongside inclined-plane laws of falling bodies.
events.impact: Overturned Aristotelian cosmology and established inertial relativity and experimental mechanics.

events.title: Astronomia Nova & Laws of Planetary Motion
events.summary: Using Tycho Brahe's precision Mars observations, proved that planets sweep equal areas in equal times along elliptical orbits and later derived the harmonic period-distance law.
events.impact: Provided the exact empirical foundation from which Newton derived inverse-square universal gravitation.

events.title: Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica
events.summary: Unified terrestrial mechanics and celestial orbits under three laws of motion and universal gravitation (F = G m₁m₂ / r²), supported by fluxional calculus.
events.impact: Defined classical physics and predictive mathematical science for over two centuries.

events.title: Euler's Equations of Fluid Dynamics & Analytical Mechanics
events.summary: Formulated the differential equations of inviscid fluid flow, rigid-body rotation, and variational calculus (Euler-Lagrange equations), recasting Newtonian mechanics in analytical form.
events.impact: Created the mathematical language of continuum mechanics, aerodynamics, and modern field theory.

events.title: Electromagnetic Induction & Field Concept
events.summary: Demonstrated that a changing magnetic flux induces an electric current in a conductor and introduced physical lines of force filling space.
events.impact: Enabled electrical generators, transformers, and the modern field paradigm of fundamental physics.

events.title: Maxwell's Equations & Light as an Electromagnetic Wave
events.summary: Published 'A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field', adding displacement current to unify electricity, magnetism, and optics, predicting electromagnetic waves traveling at speed c.
events.impact: Unified optics with electromagnetism, predicted radio waves, and directly prompted special relativity.

events.title: Statistical Entropy & Kinetic Theory of Matter
events.summary: Connected macroscopic thermodynamic entropy to microscopic atomic probability distributions via S = k_B ln W and derived the Boltzmann transport equation.
events.impact: Founded statistical mechanics and provided the probabilistic bridge between atoms and thermodynamics.

events.title: Discovery of X-Rays
events.summary: Detected penetrating invisible radiation from cathode-ray discharge tubes capable of imaging human bone structure, earning the inaugural 1901 Nobel Prize in Physics.
events.impact: Revolutionized medical diagnostics, crystallography, and synchrotron materials science.

events.title: Discovery of Polonium, Radium & Nuclear Radioactivity
events.summary: Coined the term 'radioactivity' and chemically isolated polonium and radium from pitchblende, proving radiation is an intrinsic atomic property rather than a chemical reaction.
events.impact: Opened nuclear physics and earned Marie Curie two Nobel Prizes in Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911).

events.title: Planck's Quantum Hypothesis (E = hν)
events.summary: Resolved the black-body radiation ultraviolet catastrophe by proposing that oscillators emit and absorb electromagnetic energy only in discrete quanta E = hν.
events.impact: Introduced Planck's constant h and inaugurated the quantum revolution.

events.title: Einstein's Annus Mirabilis Papers
events.summary: Published four groundbreaking papers on light quanta (photoelectric effect), Brownian motion (proving atomic reality), special relativity, and mass-energy equivalence (E = mc²).
events.impact: Dismantled absolute space and time while cementing the reality of both photons and atoms.

events.title: Discovery of the Atomic Nucleus
events.figure: Ernest Rutherford, Hans Geiger & Ernest Marsden
events.summary: Alpha-particle scattering off thin gold foil revealed occasional large-angle deflections, proving atoms consist of a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus surrounded by empty space.
events.impact: Replaced the plum-pudding model and launched nuclear and atomic quantum physics.

events.title: General Theory of Relativity
events.summary: Presented the Einstein field equations describing gravity as the geometric curvature of four-dimensional spacetime, predicting Mercury's perihelion precession, light bending, black holes, and gravitational waves.
events.impact: Became the foundation of modern cosmology, GPS timekeeping, and relativistic astrophysics.

events.title: Noether's Theorem: Symmetries & Conservation Laws
events.summary: Proved that every differentiable continuous symmetry of a physical system's action corresponds to an exact conservation law (energy, momentum, angular momentum, charge).
events.impact: Serves as the structural backbone of gauge theory, the Standard Model, and general relativity.

events.title: Fifth Solvay Congress: Electrons and Photons
events.figure: Niels Bohr, Albert Einstein, Werner Heisenberg, Erwin Schrödinger, Marie Curie & 24 Others
events.summary: Twenty-nine physicists (17 Nobel laureates) gathered in Brussels to debate the newly forged matrix and wave quantum mechanics, igniting the famous Bohr-Einstein debates on completeness and uncertainty.
events.impact: Crystallized the Copenhagen interpretation and shaped a century of quantum foundations research.

events.title: The Dirac Equation & Prediction of Antimatter
events.summary: Reconciled quantum mechanics with special relativity for the electron, naturally explaining electron spin-1/2, magnetic moment, and predicting the existence of the positron (discovered 1932).
events.impact: Laid the cornerstone for relativistic quantum field theory and antiparticle physics.

events.title: Discovery & Theoretical Explanation of Nuclear Fission
events.figure: Lise Meitner, Otto Hahn, Fritz Strassmann & Otto Frisch
events.summary: Hahn and Strassmann chemically detected barium after bombarding uranium with neutrons, while Meitner and Frisch explained the liquid-drop splitting of the nucleus and calculated its ~200 MeV energy release.
events.impact: Unlocked nuclear energy, medical isotopes, and modern nuclear physics.

events.title: Invention of the Point-Contact Transistor
events.figure: John Bardeen, Walter Brattain & William Shockley
events.summary: Demonstrated solid-state electrical signal amplification in germanium at Bell Labs using quantum band theory of semiconductors.
events.impact: Launched the microelectronics and digital computing revolution that powers modern civilization.

events.title: Renormalized Quantum Electrodynamics (QED)
events.figure: Shin'ichirō Tomonaga, Julian Schwinger, Richard Feynman & Freeman Dyson
events.summary: Developed covariant renormalization and Feynman diagrams to compute the Lamb shift and electron anomalous magnetic moment to breathtaking precision.
events.impact: Created the most accurately tested physical theory in history (matching experiment to better than 1 part in 10¹²).

events.title: Founding of CERN (European Organization for Nuclear Research)
events.summary: Ratified the CERN Convention on September 29, 1954, creating a peaceful international laboratory for fundamental particle physics on the Franco-Swiss border.
events.impact: Delivered neutral currents, W/Z bosons, the World Wide Web, antihydrogen, and the Higgs boson.

events.title: Wu Experiment: Parity Violation in Weak Interactions
events.figure: Chien-Shiung Wu (testing T. D. Lee & C. N. Yang)
events.summary: Observed asymmetric beta-decay electron emission from cryogenically polarized Cobalt-60 nuclei, proving that the weak nuclear force distinguishes left from right.
events.impact: Shattered the assumption of universal mirror symmetry and guided the V−A structure of electroweak theory.

events.title: First Working Optical Laser
events.figure: Theodore H. Maiman (building on Townes, Schawlow, Basov & Prokhorov)
events.summary: Operated a flashlamp-pumped synthetic ruby rod at Hughes Research Laboratories, emitting coherent 694.3 nm red laser light.
events.impact: Enabled fiber-optic internet, atomic clocks, laser cooling, LIGO interferometry, and fusion ignition.

events.title: Discovery of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB)
events.figure: Arno Penzias & Robert Wilson (interpreted with Dicke, Peebles, Roll & Wilkinson)
events.summary: Measured an isotropic 3.5 K microwave excess (later refined by COBE to 2.725 K) with the Holmdel Horn Antenna—the faint thermal afterglow of the hot Big Bang emitted 380,000 years after cosmic birth.
events.impact: Confirmed the Big Bang model and launched precision observational cosmology (COBE, WMAP, Planck).

events.title: Bell's Theorem & Experimental Test of Quantum Nonlocality
events.summary: Proved that no local hidden-variable theory can reproduce all statistical predictions of quantum mechanics, turning the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen paradox into a testable inequality.
events.impact: Sparked the Clauser-Aspect-Zeilinger experiments (2022 Nobel) and modern quantum information science.

events.title: Quarks, Electroweak Unification & the Standard Model
events.figure: Murray Gell-Mann, George Zweig, Sheldon Glashow, Abdus Salam, Steven Weinberg, Gross, Politzer, Wilczek, Richter & Ting
events.summary: From the 1964 quark model and Higgs mechanism through SLAC deep inelastic scattering (1968), asymptotic freedom (1973), and the November Revolution J/ψ charm discovery (1974), the SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) Standard Model crystallized.
events.impact: Unified electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions into a single predictive quantum field theory.

events.title: Discovery of the W and Z Bosons at CERN
events.figure: Carlo Rubbia, Simon van der Meer & UA1/UA2 Collaborations
events.summary: Using stochastic cooling to collide protons and antiprotons at CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron, UA1 and UA2 discovered the massive weak-force gauge bosons right at predicted masses.
events.impact: Provided decisive direct confirmation of electroweak symmetry breaking.

events.title: High-Temperature Cuprate Superconductivity
events.figure: J. Georg Bednorz & K. Alex Müller
events.summary: Discovered superconductivity at 35 K in a lanthanum barium copper oxide ceramic, soon leading to YBCO superconductors above liquid-nitrogen temperature (77 K).
events.impact: Opened strongly correlated electron physics and enabled modern 20-tesla fusion magnets.

events.title: First Gaseous Bose-Einstein Condensate
events.figure: Eric Cornell, Carl Wieman & Wolfgang Ketterle
events.summary: Cooled rubidium and sodium vapors to nanokelvin temperatures using laser and evaporative cooling, causing thousands of atoms to coalesce into a single macroscopic quantum wavefunction.
events.impact: Created ultracold quantum simulators, atom interferometers, and precision quantum sensors.

events.title: Neutrino Oscillations & Proof That Neutrinos Have Mass
events.summary: Super-Kamiokande demonstrated that atmospheric muon neutrinos change flavor in flight, followed by SNO resolving the solar neutrino problem—proving neutrinos carry non-zero mass.
events.impact: Delivered the first concrete laboratory physics beyond the original Standard Model.

events.title: Accelerating Expansion of the Universe (Dark Energy)
events.figure: Saul Perlmutter, Brian P. Schmidt & Adam G. Riess
events.summary: Distant Type Ia supernovae appeared dimmer than expected in a decelerating cosmos, revealing that cosmic expansion is accelerating under a repulsive dark energy (~68% of the universe).
events.impact: Reshaped the ΛCDM standard model of cosmology and motivated Euclid, DESI, and Rubin.

events.title: Isolation of Two-Dimensional Graphene
events.summary: Exfoliated atomically thin single-layer carbon sheets from graphite, uncovering massless Dirac fermions, anomalous room-temperature quantum Hall effects, and extraordinary tensile strength.
events.impact: Launched the entire field of 2D van der Waals heterostructures and moiré twistronics.

events.title: Discovery of the Higgs Boson (125 GeV)
events.figure: ATLAS & CMS Collaborations (predicted by Englert, Brout, Higgs, Guralnik, Hagen, Kibble)
events.summary: On July 4, 2012, ATLAS and CMS independently announced a 5-sigma spin-0 boson at 125 GeV, confirming the Brout-Englert-Higgs quantum field that gives fundamental particles mass.
events.impact: Completed the particle roster of the Standard Model and opened precision Higgs-sector physics.

events.title: First Direct Detection of Gravitational Waves (GW150914)
events.summary: On September 14, 2015, LIGO's twin 4 km laser interferometers recorded spacetime strain of 10⁻²¹ from two merging ~30-solar-mass black holes 1.3 billion light-years away.
events.impact: Opened gravitational-wave astronomy—an entirely new observational sense for the dark universe.

events.title: First Horizon-Scale Image of a Black Hole (M87*)
events.location: Global VLBI Array (anchored at ALMA, Chile)
events.summary: Linked millimeter-wave radio dishes across Earth into a planet-sized virtual telescope to resolve the glowing asymmetric photon ring around the 6.5-billion-solar-mass black hole in M87.
events.impact: Provided direct visual confirmation of strong-field general relativity at an event horizon.

events.title: James Webb Space Telescope First Deep Field
events.summary: With a 6.5 m gold-coated segmented beryllium mirror operating at 40 K, JWST unveiled galaxies shining within 300 million years of the Big Bang and detailed exoplanet atmospheric spectra.
events.impact: Transformed infrared cosmology, star-formation physics, and exoplanet characterization.

events.title: First Laboratory Controlled Fusion Ignition (Q_target > 1)
events.summary: On December 5, 2022, 192 ultraviolet laser beams delivered 2.05 MJ onto a cryogenic deuterium-tritium capsule, yielding 3.15 MJ of fusion energy (target gain ~1.54, later surpassed).
events.impact: Proved scientific breakeven of controlled inertial confinement fusion in a laboratory setting.

events.title: Vera C. Rubin Observatory First Light & LSST Survey
events.summary: Equipped with a 3.2-gigapixel camera on an 8.4 m wide-field telescope, Rubin unveiled its First Look imagery in June 2025 and began full 10-year LSST southern-sky survey operations in July 2026 to map dark matter, dark energy, and cosmic transients.
events.impact: Creates a 10-year ultra-high-definition time-lapse movie of the universe (~20 terabytes nightly).

events.title: SPARC High-Field Compact Fusion Tokamak Target Operations
events.summary: Compact 12-tesla on-axis tokamak built with 20-tesla REBCO high-temperature superconducting magnets, targeting net fusion plasma energy gain (Q > 2, up to Q ~ 11) in a fraction of ITER's volume.
events.impact: Tests whether high-field HTS magnets can accelerate commercial fusion power plants onto the 2030s grid.

events.title: Hyper-Kamiokande Operations Begin
events.summary: A 260,000-ton ultrapure water Cherenkov detector—over 5× Super-Kamiokande's volume—entering photosensor installation in 2027 and scientific operations in 2028 to measure leptonic CP violation, supernova neutrinos, and proton decay.
events.impact: Probes why matter triumphed over antimatter in the early universe and tests Grand Unified Theories.

events.title: ESO Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) First Light
events.summary: The world's largest optical/near-infrared telescope featuring a 39.3-meter primary mirror composed of 798 hexagonal segments—targeted for mirror installation in 2028 and technical first light in 2029 to directly image rocky exoplanets.
events.impact: Will collect 100 million times more light than the human eye, probing exoplanet biosignatures and cosmic acceleration directly.

events.title: Square Kilometre Array (SKAO) Full Science Operations
events.summary: Twin continental radio telescope arrays—197 dishes in South Africa (SKA-Mid) and 131,072 dipole antennas in Western Australia (SKA-Low)—delivering unprecedented radio sensitivity.
events.impact: Will map the Cosmic Dawn 21-cm hydrogen signal, test general relativity with pulsars, and probe cosmic magnetism.

events.title: DUNE (Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment) Beam Operations
events.summary: Fires the world's most intense neutrino beam 1,300 km through Earth's crust from Fermilab to 70,000 tons of liquid argon detectors 1.5 km underground at SURF in South Dakota.
events.impact: Determines the neutrino mass ordering, searches for CP violation, and watches neutron star birth via core-collapse neutrinos.

events.title: LISA Space Gravitational-Wave Observatory Launch
events.location: Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Orbit (2.5 Million km Arms)
events.summary: Three spacecraft flying in a 2.5-million-kilometer equilateral triangle linked by picometer-precision laser interferometry to listen to millihertz gravitational waves from supermassive black hole mergers.
events.impact: Extends gravitational-wave astronomy across the entire observable universe to cosmic redshift z > 20.

events.title: ITER Research Operations & Burning Plasma Campaign
events.summary: Under the updated 2024 ITER baseline, full magnetic-energy plasma operations begin in the mid-2030s leading into deuterium-tritium burning plasma targeting 500 MW fusion output from 50 MW input (Q = 10).
events.impact: Demonstrates reactor-scale burning-plasma physics, tritium breeding modules, and integrated fusion engineering.

events.title: Einstein Telescope Underground Gravitational-Wave Observatory
events.summary: A proposed third-generation European underground observatory with 10 km cryogenic laser arms buried 200–300 m below ground to slash seismic and thermal noise by an order of magnitude.
events.impact: Will detect hundreds of thousands of binary black hole and neutron star mergers per year back to the dark ages.

events.title: Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee) Precision Higgs Factory
events.summary: Proposed 90.7 km underground tunnel beneath the Geneva basin starting with an electron-positron Higgs, electroweak, and top-quark factory (FCC-ee) in the mid-2040s, paving the way for a 100 TeV proton collider (FCC-hh).
events.impact: Pushes precision measurements of the Higgs self-coupling and searches for new physics far beyond LHC reach.
